data.name: The Hanged Man
data.detailed_description:
"You're a demon child.

Someday, you'll be burning in hell for your sins."

This is the fourth and final title in the Strange Man series, developed by Uri Games.

In The Hanged Man, you play as William Morton, a young boy wandering around a town in the snow. As he wanders to and fro, he takes cover in an abandoned building with his best buddy, a mouse named Pop.

Although he hopes to leave the building soon, Pop disappears into the building, leaving William alone. William must now gather his courage and head further into the building, seeking out his only friend.

What secrets lie hidden within?

The Steam version features special additions such as achievements and multi-language localization.

Features

  • 2D horror-adventure featuring exploration and action elements

  • Wide range of hardcore expressions of violence

  • Multiple endings

reviews.review:
The Hanged Man is a story-driven psychological horror adventure that builds its identity around loneliness, childhood trauma, mystery, and an increasingly uncomfortable sense that something is deeply wrong. Developed by Uri Games and published by PLAYISM, it is the fourth and concluding entry in the Strange Man series. Its pixel-art presentation may appear simple at first, but the game uses that simplicity effectively, creating tension through dark environments, unsettling discoveries, disturbing imagery, and the vulnerability of its young protagonist rather than relying on technical spectacle.

The story centers on William Morton, a troubled boy who arrives in a snowy town accompanied by his small mouse companion, Pop. After taking refuge inside an abandoned building, William becomes separated from Pop and begins searching for him. What initially seems like a relatively straightforward objective soon draws him farther into an environment filled with danger, strange encounters, and uncomfortable reminders of his past. William is not presented as a conventional horror protagonist capable of confidently confronting whatever appears before him. His age, emotional instability, and personal history make him feel vulnerable, which gives the darker moments considerably more impact.

Most of the gameplay revolves around exploring rooms, examining objects, collecting useful items, solving environmental problems, and progressing through conversations and scripted events. There are moments involving more immediate danger, but action is not the primary attraction. The Hanged Man belongs firmly to the traditional narrative-focused pixel horror style, where curiosity and careful investigation matter more than combat skill. The puzzles generally exist to maintain interaction and encourage exploration rather than overwhelm the player with complicated logic.

Atmosphere is one of the game's strongest qualities. The abandoned interiors are intentionally sparse and gloomy, allowing ordinary rooms and corridors to become threatening simply because the player does not know what might be waiting ahead. The pixel graphics leave some horrific details to the imagination, yet the game is not afraid to employ explicit or violent imagery when appropriate. This balance between suggestion and direct confrontation prevents the horror from depending entirely on jump scares. Silence, isolation, strange characters, and William's emotional condition contribute just as much to the discomfort.

The narrative gradually becomes more important than the immediate mystery of finding Pop. William's fears, memories, relationships, and perception of himself become intertwined with the supernatural events surrounding him. The game explores ideas involving guilt, rejection, punishment, friendship, and personal identity without abandoning its horror framework. Some events are deliberately difficult to interpret when first encountered, encouraging the player to continue until later revelations provide additional context. Players familiar with the earlier Strange Man titles will also recognize connections that help make this installment feel like a genuine conclusion rather than an unrelated sequel.

Multiple endings give the adventure some replay value. Decisions and actions can influence how William's journey concludes, making another playthrough worthwhile for anyone interested in seeing the full range of outcomes. There are also 28 Steam achievements for completionists. These additions fit a relatively compact narrative game well because they provide reasons to investigate situations differently without artificially extending the central storyline.

The Steam release includes English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese interface and subtitle options, with full English voice acting also available. The voice work adds personality to important exchanges while preserving the deliberately old-fashioned visual presentation. System requirements are extremely modest, and the installation requires only a small amount of storage, so the game should run comfortably on a wide range of Windows PCs.

Steam Deck compatibility does not currently have an official Valve Verified or Playable designation, so it should be considered unverified rather than guaranteed. Given the game's lightweight technical requirements and relatively straightforward controls, running it through Proton may be possible, but the absence of an official compatibility rating means players should not assume every aspect will work perfectly without adjustments.

The largest drawback is that the gameplay itself is relatively basic. Movement, object interaction, and puzzle solving can feel dated beside modern horror adventures, while players seeking elaborate combat or complex mechanical systems will find little of that here. The pixel-art aesthetic is similarly dependent on personal taste. What compensates for these limitations is the game's commitment to character-driven horror. Its best scenes work because the frightening circumstances have emotional significance for William rather than existing merely to provide monsters or sudden shocks.

As the finale of the Strange Man series, The Hanged Man delivers a compact but memorable combination of psychological horror, exploration, puzzles, disturbing imagery, and emotional storytelling. Its mechanics are modest, yet its unsettling atmosphere and vulnerable protagonist give the adventure considerably more personality than its simple presentation initially suggests. It is especially worthwhile for players who enjoy classic indie horror games where uncovering a character's history is every bit as important as surviving the threats hidden in the darkness.

Rating: 8/10
